chains.title: NME2 binds the alt allele more strongly and may act on CYP7A1
chains.element: Same candidate unannotated distal element: no ENCODE cCRE overlaps the variant, nearest CA-H3K4me3 cCRE 1544 bp away, no VEP regulatory feature.
chains.cell_type: Hep 3B2.1-7 liver cancer line; NME2 is highly expressed there (928.15 TPM, rank 1/1626 TFs).

links.claim: NME2 is predicted by QBiC-SELEX to bind the alt T allele more strongly: own model z=28.95, effect=0.573 (alt > ref). No ENCODE NME2 ChIP-seq peak is reported over this variant in the matching liver biosample, though absence can mean no NME2 experiment there; occupancy is therefore unknown. This is SELEX-only evidence.

The variant sits in a noncoding region with no ENCODE cCRE overlap; the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away and VEP reports no regulatory feature. It is only a candidate unannotated element, not an established active regulatory element.

CYP7A1 lies 926.8 kb downstream of the variant, but there is no eQTL for this variant in GTEx, and Open Targets reports no association between CYP7A1 and free cholesterol in large LDL. The target-gene link is distal and speculative.

NME2 is extremely highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (928.15 TPM, rank 1/1626 TFs), so it could occupy an accessible site in liver cells if one exists, but there is no direct occupancy evidence at this variant.

Alt T is predicted to increase NME2 binding and could alter CYP7A1 expression and LDL cholesterol, but there is no GWAS Catalog, Open Targets, or GTEx eQTL support for rs7001688 and LDL cholesterol. The phenotype link is unsupported.

chains.title: CASZ1 binds the alt allele more strongly and may act on FAM110B
chains.element: Candidate unannotated distal element: no ENCODE cCRE overlaps the variant; nearest cCRE is CA-H3K4me3 1544 bp away, and VEP reports no regulatory feature.

links.claim: CASZ1 is predicted by QBiC-SELEX to bind the alt T allele more strongly: own model z=32.75, effect=2.741 (alt > ref). ENCODE has never assayed CASZ1 here, so occupancy is unknown; CASZ1 expression is low in Hep 3B2.1-7 (4.18 TPM). This is SELEX-only binding evidence and is weak without occupancy.

The variant sits in a noncoding region with no ENCODE cCRE overlap; the nearest cCRE is a CA-H3K4me3 1544 bp away, and VEP reports no regulatory feature. This is only a candidate unannotated element, not an established active regulatory element.

FAM110B is the closest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb upstream, but distance is very indirect; GTEx reports no significant eQTL for this variant, and the Europe PMC hit is a keyword match that does not establish a mechanistic FAM110B-LDL link.

Hep 3B2.1-7 is a liver-cancer line, and CASZ1 is expressed there at low level (4.18 TPM), but there is no evidence that CASZ1 occupies this site in liver cells or that this line is the relevant LDL context.

Alt T is predicted to increase CASZ1 binding and, through FAM110B, alter LDL cholesterol, but there is no GWAS Catalog, Open Targets, or GTEx eQTL support connecting rs7001688 to LDL cholesterol. The phenotype link is speculative.

chains.title: TCF20 binds the ref allele more strongly and may act on FAM110B

links.claim: TCF20 is predicted by QBiC-SELEX to bind the ref G allele more strongly: own model z=-20.49, effect=-0.151 (ref > alt). The effect is small, and E16 reports a higher alt site-strength percentile despite the negative effect, so the direction/strength is internally inconsistent. ENCODE has never assayed TCF20 here, so occupancy is unknown.

The variant sits in a noncoding region with no ENCODE cCRE overlap; the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away and VEP reports no regulatory feature. It is only a candidate unannotated element, not an established active regulatory element.

FAM110B is the closest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb upstream, but distance is very indirect; GTEx reports no significant eQTL for this variant, and E09 does not establish a verified FAM110B-LDL mechanism.
Hep 3B2.1-7 expresses TCF20 at 23.44 TPM, so TCF20 could act in this liver-cancer context if the site is occupied, but there is no occupancy evidence at this variant.

Higher ref G binding of TCF20 may repress or activate FAM110B; alt T would lower TCF20 binding, but the direction of any LDL effect is unknown. There is no GWAS Catalog, Open Targets, or GTEx eQTL support for rs7001688 and LDL cholesterol.
